sections.content: How many people stayed in Hale (Trafford) after gaining qualifications?

Hale (Trafford) is a small town in the North West. Hale (Trafford) does not have its own university.

Hale (Trafford) has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Hale (Trafford) ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 665 state-school pupils from Hale (Trafford) who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 465 (70%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 130 (20%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Hale (Trafford) to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Hale (Trafford)'s pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Hale (Trafford) in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Hale (Trafford) move to?

Of Hale (Trafford)'s graduates, 220 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 80 of those graduates (36%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Hale (Trafford)'s qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 50 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 35 of those qualified non-graduates (70%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Hale (Trafford)'s GCSE cohort:

  • 125 graduates left the North West
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 15% of graduates living in Hale (Trafford) had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 275 graduates from our cohort living in Hale (Trafford), compared with the 465 graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 87% of graduates had sat their GCSEs in Hale (Trafford), while 15% had moved there from elsewhere.
